title: Potential finite smooth cover of a separated flat group over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and let $G$ be a group scheme over $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with multiplication, identity section and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Assume $G\to S$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exist a faithfully flat injective local homomorphism $R\to R'$ of discrete valuation rings and an $R'$-group scheme $N$, separated and of finite type and smooth over $R'$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], together with an $R'$-group homomorphism $q:N\to G_{R'}=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}R'$ [def-pc-base-change], such that $q$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The ring $R'$ can be chosen strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with algebraically closed residue field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. No affineness or generic smoothness or connectedness hypothesis on $G$ is imposed, and no excellence hypothesis on $R$ is imposed. Faithfully flat has the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]; local means that the maximal ideal of $R$ maps into that of $R'$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to S$ is flat and surjective and is a singleton fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering].

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/qrg.pdf: Proposition 3.1, first paragraph, printed p.5; Appendix Corollary A.4, printed p.29, including stability under further Dedekind extensions; the henselian extension with algebraically closed residue field used after Lemma A.9, printed pp.31-32. Use the finite normalization of the reduced base change, not the potentially non-finite ordinary smoothening of an arbitrary model.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$ and an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of its residue field. The flat local extension with prescribed residue field gives a local flat $R$-algebra $T$ with maximal ideal $\pi T$ and residue field $\bar k$. Tensoring the injection $R\xrightarrow{\pi}R$ with $T$ shows that $\pi$ is a nonzerodivisor on $T$. The principal-regular-local completion lemma therefore gives a complete DVR $D=\varprojlim T/\pi^nT$ with uniformizer the image of $\pi$ and residue field $\bar k$. The composite $R\to D$ is local and injective: every nonzero $a\in R$ is $u\pi^n$ for a unit $u$, whose image is nonzero in the domain $D$.

source.place: Tags 03C3 (lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field) and 0328 (lemma-cohen-rings-exist), completion argument generalized to a regular generator; no excellence of R is used.

proof.text: Set $X=G_D$. Flatness, separatedness and finite type persist under this base change by the three cited permanence statements. The group maps of $G$ also base change: the universal property identifies $(G\times_RG)_D$ with $G_D\times_DG_D$, and base change carries each group-diagram equality to the same equality on $X$. Thus $X$ satisfies the hypotheses of the complete-trait normalized-reduction theorem. Apply it and obtain $L/\operatorname{Frac}D$, its complete DVR $V$, the reduction $H=(G_V)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and $\nu:N\to H$. In particular $H,N$ are flat separated finite-type $V$-schemes, $\nu$ is finite surjective, $H_L$ is geometrically reduced, and $N_k$ is geometrically reduced for $k=V/\mathfrak m_V$.

source.place: Appendix Theorem A.2 and Remark A.3; Stacks Tag 09IL, theorem-normalized-base-change-with-reduced-fibre, after passage to the complete DVR D.

proof.text: Base change along $D\to V$ once more: $G_V=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}D}\operatorname{Spec}V$ is flat, separated and of finite type over $V$ by the same three permanence statements, and, as in Step 2, the identification $(X\times_DX)_V=G_V\times_VG_V$ carries the group maps and group-diagram equalities of $X$ to $G_V$; moreover $H=(G_V)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Apply the group-structure lemma to this $V$-group $G_V$ and this $H,N,\nu$. Its finite-normalization, flatness of $H,N$ and two geometric-reducedness hypotheses are precisely the conclusions of Step 2. It equips $H$ and $N$ with compatible $V$-group structures and identifies $N_L$ with $H_L$ as groups. Consequently both $N_L$ and $N_k$ are geometrically reduced groups of finite type over their respective fields. The geometrically-reduced-group smoothness lemma makes both fibres smooth. This step uses neither an affine coordinate Hopf algebra nor connectedness of the fibres.

source.place: Corollary A.4 proof, printed p.29; smoothness of geometric fibres by Stacks groupoids.tex Tags 047N and 047P.

proof.text: The scheme $N$ is flat and of finite type over the Noetherian ring $V$. On each affine chart its coordinate algebra is finitely generated over $V$, hence finitely presented by the finite-type-over-Noetherian finite-presentation lemma. Thus $N\to\operatorname{Spec}V$ is locally of finite presentation. A DVR has just its generic and closed points, whose fibres are smooth by Step 3. The flat, locally finitely presented, smooth-fibre criterion proves that $N$ is smooth over $V$. It is already separated and of finite type by Step 2.

source.place: Tag 01V8, lemma-smooth-flat-smooth-fibres; Tag 02H6 identifies the smoothness conventions. Finite presentation is checked on affine charts.

proof.text: Define $q$ as $N\xrightarrow{\nu}H\xrightarrow{j}G_V$. The reduction inclusion $j$ is a surjective closed immersion by the reduction theorem and is finite by the closed-immersion lemma. The finite-composition lemma makes $q$ finite; its underlying map is surjective because both factors are surjective. The group structures of Step 3 make both factors homomorphisms, so their composite commutes with multiplication, identity and inverse by composing those equalities. This is the required finite surjective group homomorphism.

source.place: Reduction and finite-morphism composition; Corollary A.4 applied as in the first paragraph of Proposition 3.1, printed p.5.

proof.text: Take $R'=V$. The local injection $R\to D\to V$ makes $V$ torsion free as an $R$-module; the PID torsion-free-flat lemma makes it flat. The flat-local lemma then makes it faithfully flat and gives surjectivity of $\operatorname{Spec}V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. The affine flatness criterion gives flatness of this scheme morphism. Its singleton is an fpqc cover directly from the definition: the only nonempty opens of the spectrum of a DVR are the whole spectrum and its generic point; their inverse images are respectively the affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}V$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}V$, which surject onto those opens. The empty open uses the empty family.

source.place: Tags 0AUW and 0539 for torsion-free flatness; flat-local faithful flatness, followed by the explicit two-open fpqc verification.

proof.text: Finally $V$ is complete for its maximal ideal, so the complete-pair lemma makes it henselian. Since $V$ is finite over $D$, its residue field is finite-dimensional over $D/\mathfrak m_D=\bar k$ (reduce any finite set of module generators). This field extension is an isomorphism, since $\bar k$ is algebraically closed. In particular the residue field is separably closed, and the henselian-terminology definition says that $V$ is strictly henselian. Together with Steps 4--6 this proves every clause without any excellence, affineness, generic smoothness or connectedness assumption on $G$.
